definition_title: Weighted ideals and coefficient packets for multivariate power series
natural_language_statement: For a commutative ring R and a weight w : σ → ℕ, weightedIdeal w N consists of multivariate power series whose weighted order is at least N. Membership is characterized by vanishing of every coefficient indexed by a finitely supported multi-index of weighted degree below N. Products of weighted ideals add their thresholds, and if I ≤ weightedIdeal w R₀ then Iⁿ ≤ weightedIdeal w (n R₀). For rational nonnegative weights v : σ → ℚ, rationalWeightedIdeal v hv H consists of series whose coefficients vanish at all multi-indices of v-weight below H; these ideals also multiply by adding thresholds, and their powers obey the corresponding bound under the stated ideal containment. coordinatePowerIdeal e is the ideal generated by the coordinate powers Xᵢ^(e i). RationalCoefficientPacket v H is the function type from multi-indices of v-weight below H to R, and rationalCoefficientPacket evaluates a series' coefficients on that domain.
explanation: These declarations express order conditions on multivariate power series as ideal membership and coefficient vanishing. The multiplication and power-containment results provide threshold bookkeeping for both natural-number and rational weights. The packet definitions record precisely the coefficients below a rational weighted threshold; no surjectivity claim is included in this provider bundle.
